### Chapter 24: Benchmarks and Active Risk {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: sol-24-setup
#| include: false
source("R/_common.R")
library(tidypm)
library(knitr)

R  <- as_xts_pm(sim_class_returns_monthly, date, class, return)
rf <- sim_riskfree_monthly$return
Re <- R - rf
stopifnot(ncol(Re) == 16L, !anyNA(Re), length(rf) == nrow(R))

# The chapter's policy benchmark, manager, return series and measures, repeated
# so that this fragment runs on its own.
sleeve_of <- function(a) dplyr::case_when(
  grepl("_equity$", a)     ~ "equity",
  grepl("_government$", a) ~ "government",
  grepl("_credit$", a)     ~ "credit",
  TRUE                     ~ "commodity")
sleeve_policy <- c(equity = 0.50, government = 0.30, credit = 0.15, commodity = 0.05)
sl <- sleeve_of(colnames(R))
b  <- setNames(sleeve_policy[sl] / as.numeric(table(sl)[sl]), colnames(R))
stopifnot(abs(sum(b) - 1) < 1e-12, identical(names(b), colnames(R)))

win <- 60L
spec_mv <- portfolio.spec(assets = colnames(Re)) |>
  add.constraint(type = "full_investment") |>
  add.constraint(type = "long_only") |>
  add.objective(type = "risk", name = "var")
bt <- optimize.portfolio.rebalancing(
  Re, spec_mv, optimize_method = "ROI",
  rebalance_on = "months", training_period = win, rolling_window = win - 1L)
W_act <- extractWeights(bt)
stopifnot(all(diagnose_rebalancing(bt)$status == "converged"),
          identical(colnames(W_act), colnames(R)))

first_w <- zoo::index(W_act)[1]
R_oos   <- R[zoo::index(R) > first_w]
rf_oos  <- xts::xts(rf[zoo::index(R) > first_w], order.by = zoo::index(R_oos))
Rp <- Return.portfolio(R_oos, weights = W_act)
Rb <- Return.portfolio(R_oos, weights = b, rebalance_on = "months")
colnames(Rp) <- "active"; colnames(Rb) <- "policy"
W_used <- zoo::coredata(W_act)[-nrow(W_act), ]
stopifnot(nrow(W_used) == nrow(R_oos),
          all.equal(as.numeric(Rp), rowSums(W_used * zoo::coredata(R_oos))),
          all.equal(as.numeric(Rb), as.numeric(zoo::coredata(R_oos) %*% b)))
a <- Rp - Rb
colnames(a) <- "active_return"

te_pa <- TrackingError(Rp, Rb)
ir_ar <- InformationRatio(Rp, Rb, geometric = FALSE)
stopifnot(all.equal(as.numeric(ir_ar), mean(a) / stats::sd(a) * sqrt(12)))

# The Brinson chunk of the chapter, with the benchmark as an argument so that a
# second yardstick can be attributed against without repeating it.
sleeves  <- sort(unique(sl))
W_used_x <- xts::xts(W_used, order.by = zoo::index(R_oos))
brinson_against <- function(b) {
  brinson_month <- function(t) {
    r <- as.numeric(R_oos[t, ]); w <- as.numeric(W_used_x[t, ]); r_b <- sum(b * r)
    out <- vapply(sleeves, function(s) {
      i  <- sl == s
      bs <- sum(b[i]); ws <- sum(w[i])
      beta_s <- sum(b[i] * r[i]) / bs
      r_s    <- if (ws > 1e-10) sum(w[i] * r[i]) / ws else beta_s
      c(allocation  = (ws - bs) * (beta_s - r_b),
        selection   = bs * (r_s - beta_s),
        interaction = (ws - bs) * (r_s - beta_s))
    }, numeric(3))
    t(out)
  }
  effects <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(R_oos)), brinson_month)
  stopifnot(all.equal(vapply(effects, sum, numeric(1)),
                      as.numeric(Rp) - as.numeric(zoo::coredata(R_oos) %*% b)))
  attribution <- Reduce(`+`, effects) / length(effects) * 12
  tibble::tibble(sleeve = sleeves,
                 held   = as.numeric(tapply(colMeans(W_used), sl, sum)[sleeves]),
                 policy = as.numeric(tapply(b, sl, sum)[sleeves]),
                 allocation  = attribution[, "allocation"],
                 selection   = attribution[, "selection"],
                 interaction = attribution[, "interaction"]) |>
    dplyr::mutate(total = allocation + selection + interaction)
}
attr_tbl <- brinson_against(b)
stopifnot(abs(sum(attr_tbl$total) - mean(a) * 12) < 1e-10,
          all.equal(attr_tbl$policy, as.numeric(sleeve_policy[sleeves])))

# Moments, the tracking-error tilt, and the frontier it is measured against.
mu <- colMeans(Re); S <- stats::cov(Re)
p_vol <- function(w) sqrt(as.numeric(t(w) %*% S %*% w)) * sqrt(12)
p_ret <- function(w) sum(mu * w) * 12
p_te  <- function(w) p_vol(w - b)
p_ar  <- function(w) p_ret(w - b)

te_tilt <- function(tau, sigma_max = NULL) {
  w <- CVXR::Variable(length(mu))
  x <- w - b
  cons <- list(sum(w) == 1, w >= 0,
               CVXR::quad_form(x, S) <= (tau / sqrt(12))^2)
  if (!is.null(sigma_max))
    cons <- c(cons, CVXR::quad_form(w, S) <= (sigma_max / sqrt(12))^2)
  problem <- CVXR::Problem(CVXR::Maximize(t(mu) %*% x), cons)
  CVXR::psolve(problem, solver = "CLARABEL")
  stopifnot(CVXR::status(problem) == "optimal")
  setNames(as.numeric(CVXR::value(w)), colnames(Re))
}

ef <- create.EfficientFrontier(
  Re,
  portfolio.spec(assets = colnames(Re)) |>
    add.constraint(type = "full_investment") |>
    add.constraint(type = "long_only") |>
    add.objective(type = "return", name = "mean") |>
    add.objective(type = "risk",   name = "StdDev"),
  type = "mean-StdDev", n.portfolios = 100)
fr <- as.data.frame(unclass(ef$frontier))
frontier_ret_at <- function(v) stats::approx(fr$StdDev * sqrt(12), fr$mean * 12, xout = v)$y

# The capitalization shares of the cap-weights chunk.
eq  <- sim_assets$asset_id[sim_assets$asset_class == "equity"]
Ra  <- as_xts_pm(sim_asset_returns_monthly[sim_asset_returns_monthly$asset %in% eq, ],
                 date, asset, return)
stopifnot(identical(zoo::index(Ra), zoo::index(R)), ncol(Ra) == length(eq))
cap <- sim_marketcap_weekly[sim_marketcap_weekly$asset %in% eq, ] |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = asset, values_from = market_cap) |>
  dplyr::arrange(date)
capm <- zoo::na.locf(as.matrix(cap[, colnames(Ra)]), na.rm = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(capm), colnames(Ra)))
cutoff <- c(zoo::index(R)[1] - 40, zoo::index(R)[-nrow(R)])
Wc <- capm[findInterval(cutoff, cap$date), , drop = FALSE]
Wc[is.na(Wc)] <- 0
Wc <- Wc / rowSums(Wc)
region <- sim_assets$region[match(colnames(Ra), sim_assets$asset_id)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(region))
share <- vapply(c("CH", "EU", "JP", "UK", "US"),
                function(rg) rowSums(Wc[, region == rg, drop = FALSE]), numeric(nrow(Wc)))
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(share) - 1) < 1e-10))
eq_cls <- paste0(colnames(share), "_equity")
stopifnot(all(eq_cls %in% colnames(R)))

# The error bar of the chapter.
Tn   <- nrow(a)
ir_m <- mean(a) / stats::sd(a)
se_m <- sqrt((1 + ir_m^2 / 2) / Tn)
ci   <- (ir_m + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_m) * sqrt(12)
```

#### Exercise 1

```{r}
#| label: sol-24-ex1
b_ew  <- setNames(rep(1 / ncol(R), ncol(R)), colnames(R))
Rb_ew <- Return.portfolio(R_oos, weights = b_ew, rebalance_on = "months")
colnames(Rb_ew) <- "equal_weight"
stopifnot(all.equal(as.numeric(Rb_ew), rowMeans(zoo::coredata(R_oos))))
te_ew <- TrackingError(Rp, Rb_ew)
ir_ew <- InformationRatio(Rp, Rb_ew, geometric = FALSE)
attr_ew <- brinson_against(b_ew)
stopifnot(te_ew < te_pa, ir_ew > ir_ar)
round(c(TE_policy = te_pa, TE_equal_weight = te_ew,
        IR_policy = ir_ar, IR_equal_weight = ir_ew), 3)

dplyr::bind_rows(policy = attr_tbl, `equal weight` = attr_ew, .id = "benchmark") |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(held, policy), ~ sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * .x)),
                dplyr::across(c(allocation, selection, interaction, total),
                              ~ sprintf("%+.2f%%", 100 * .x))) |>
  kable(align = "llrrrrrr")

# no sleeve changes sign; the one that moves most is the one to split
stopifnot(identical(sign(attr_ew$allocation), sign(attr_tbl$allocation)))
moved <- attr_ew$sleeve[which.max(abs(attr_ew$allocation - attr_tbl$allocation))]

# the allocation term of one sleeve, split into its level and its timing:
# (mean w_s - b_s) * mean(beta_s - r_b)  +  cov(w_s, beta_s - r_b)
pieces <- function(b, s = moved) {
  i <- sl == s; ws <- rowSums(W_used[, i, drop = FALSE]); bs <- sum(b[i])
  d <- as.numeric(zoo::coredata(R_oos)[, i, drop = FALSE] %*% (b[i] / bs)) -
       as.numeric(zoo::coredata(R_oos) %*% b)
  c(overweight = mean(ws) - bs, relative_return = mean(d) * 12,
    level  = (mean(ws) - bs) * mean(d) * 12,
    timing = mean((ws - mean(ws)) * (d - mean(d))) * 12)
}
cr <- rbind(policy = pieces(b), `equal weight` = pieces(b_ew))
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(cr[, c("level", "timing")]) -
                  c(attr_tbl$allocation[attr_tbl$sleeve == moved],
                    attr_ew$allocation[attr_ew$sleeve == moved])) < 1e-12),
          all(cr[, "overweight"] > 0), all(cr[, "relative_return"] < 0),
          all(cr[, "level"] < 0), all(cr[, "timing"] < 0),
          abs(cr["equal weight", "level"]) < abs(cr["policy", "level"]))
held_moved <- stats::quantile(rowSums(W_used[, sl == moved, drop = FALSE]), c(0.5, 1))
round(cr, 4)

moves <- c(total       = sum(attr_ew$total)       - sum(attr_tbl$total),
           benchmark   = mean(Rb - Rb_ew) * 12,
           allocation  = sum(attr_ew$allocation)  - sum(attr_tbl$allocation),
           selection   = sum(attr_ew$selection)   - sum(attr_tbl$selection),
           interaction = sum(attr_ew$interaction) - sum(attr_tbl$interaction))
stopifnot(abs(moves[["total"]] - moves[["benchmark"]]) < 1e-12,
          abs(moves[["total"]] - moves[["allocation"]]) < 1e-12,
          abs(moves[["selection"]] + moves[["interaction"]]) < 1e-12)
round(moves, 4)
```

Against equal weighting the tracking error falls from
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * te_pa)` to `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * te_ew)` and
the information ratio rises from `r sprintf("%.2f", ir_ar)` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", ir_ew)`, because a benchmark with
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * attr_ew$policy[attr_ew$sleeve == "equity"])` in
equities is closer to a manager holding
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * attr_tbl$held[attr_tbl$sleeve == "equity"])` than
one with `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sleeve_policy[["equity"]])`. No sleeve's
allocation effect changes sign: the overweight in government bonds and the
underweight in equities cost under both benchmarks, and the underweight in
credit pays under both. The `r moved` line is the one that moves most, from
`r sprintf("%+.2f%%", 100 * attr_tbl$allocation[attr_tbl$sleeve == moved])` to
`r sprintf("%+.2f%%", 100 * attr_ew$allocation[attr_ew$sleeve == moved])`,
and the split above says why. The sleeve trailed both benchmarks, by
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * abs(cr["policy", "relative_return"]))` percentage
points a year against the policy and
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * abs(cr["equal weight", "relative_return"]))` against
equal weighting, so being overweight it cost under both, and it cost less
against equal weighting, `r sprintf("%+.2f", 100 * cr["equal weight", "level"])`
points against `r sprintf("%+.2f", 100 * cr["policy", "level"])`, because the
overweight is nearly the same,
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * cr["equal weight", "overweight"])` points against
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * cr["policy", "overweight"])`, while the benchmark it
trails is the one that earns less. The timing part is small and costs under
both, `r sprintf("%+.2f", 100 * cr["policy", "timing"])` and
`r sprintf("%+.2f", 100 * cr["equal weight", "timing"])` points, because the
manager, which holds `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * held_moved[[1]])` in
`r moved` bonds in the median month and up to
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * held_moved[[2]])` at the peak, held more of them in
the months they did worst. The
total moves by exactly `r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * moves[["total"]])` percentage
points, the difference between the two benchmarks' returns, because the
manager is unchanged and the active return is $r^p - r^b$. All of it lands in
the allocation line, since
$\sum_s (w_s - b_s)(\beta_s - r^b) = \sum_s w_s \beta_s - r^b$ once the
weights sum to one, and the segment benchmarks $\beta_s$ are the same equally
weighted sleeves under both policies. Selection and interaction move by
`r sprintf("%+.2f", 100 * moves[["selection"]])` and
`r sprintf("%+.2f", 100 * moves[["interaction"]])` points, equal and opposite,
because their sum $\sum_s w_s (r_s - \beta_s)$ does not contain the benchmark's
sleeve weights at all: changing the benchmark relabels a little selection as
interaction and back, and nothing else.

#### Exercise 2

```{r}
#| label: sol-24-ex2
bound <- 1.1 * p_vol(b)
ex2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(0.02, 0.04, 0.06), function(tau) {
  w_free <- te_tilt(tau); w_bnd <- te_tilt(tau, sigma_max = bound)
  tibble::tibble(tau = tau,
                 vol_budget_only  = p_vol(w_free), vol_with_bound = p_vol(w_bnd),
                 risk_bound_binds = p_vol(w_free) > bound + 1e-6,
                 te_with_bound    = p_te(w_bnd),
                 gap_budget_only  = frontier_ret_at(p_vol(w_free)) - p_ret(w_free),
                 gap_with_bound   = frontier_ret_at(p_vol(w_bnd)) - p_ret(w_bnd),
                 IR_with_bound    = p_ar(w_bnd) / p_te(w_bnd),
                 sharpe_with_bound = p_ret(w_bnd) / p_vol(w_bnd))
}))
# the budget below which the unbounded tilt already respects the bound
tau_cross <- stats::uniroot(function(tau) p_vol(te_tilt(tau)) - bound,
                            c(0.001, 0.02), tol = 1e-5)$root
stopifnot(all(ex2$risk_bound_binds),                   # at all three budgets
          abs(ex2$gap_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.06]) < 1e-4,   # on the frontier at six
          ex2$te_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.06] < 0.06 - 1e-4,  # with the budget slack
          all(diff(ex2$sharpe_with_bound) > 0), all(diff(ex2$IR_with_bound) < 0))
ex2 |>
  dplyr::transmute(budget = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * tau),
                   `vol, budget only` = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * vol_budget_only),
                   `vol, with bound`  = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * vol_with_bound),
                   binds = risk_bound_binds,
                   `TE used` = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * te_with_bound),
                   `gap, budget only` = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * gap_budget_only),
                   `gap, with bound`  = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * dplyr::if_else(
                     abs(gap_with_bound) < 1e-6, 0, gap_with_bound)),   # zero at solver tolerance
                   IR = sprintf("%.3f", IR_with_bound),
                   Sharpe = sprintf("%.3f", sharpe_with_bound)) |>
  kable(align = "rrrlrrrrr")
c(bound = bound, budget_where_bound_starts_binding = tau_cross)
```

The bound is `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * bound)` of annual volatility, and it
binds at all three budgets: the unbounded tilt already reaches
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * ex2$vol_budget_only[ex2$tau == 0.02])` at a two
percent budget, and it stops binding only below a budget of
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * tau_cross)`, where the direction of
@eq-24-roll-solution has not yet added a tenth to the benchmark's volatility.
Relative to the frontier the bound does more work the larger the budget. The
gap of the budget-only portfolio is
`r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * ex2$gap_budget_only[ex2$tau == 0.02])`,
`r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * ex2$gap_budget_only[ex2$tau == 0.04])` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * ex2$gap_budget_only[ex2$tau == 0.06])` percentage
points at two, four and six percent; with the bound it is
`r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * ex2$gap_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.02])`,
`r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * ex2$gap_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.04])` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * abs(ex2$gap_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.06]))`. At six
percent the constrained portfolio is the frontier portfolio at the bound's
volatility, and the tracking-error budget is the constraint that has gone
slack: the portfolio uses `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * ex2$te_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.06])`
of its six. From there on a larger budget changes nothing, because the mandate
has become the maximum-return problem at a volatility cap, and the benchmark
no longer enters it. Along the way the Sharpe ratio rises from
`r sprintf("%.3f", ex2$sharpe_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.02])` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", ex2$sharpe_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.06])` while the
information ratio falls from
`r sprintf("%.3f", ex2$IR_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.02])` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", ex2$IR_with_bound[ex2$tau == 0.06])`, which is the
trade-off of @tbl-24-jorion at three budgets instead of one.

#### Exercise 3

```{r}
#| label: sol-24-ex3
a_ew <- Rb_ew - Rb                              # 1/N against the policy, same months
stopifnot(nrow(a_ew) == Tn)
ir_m_ew <- mean(a_ew) / stats::sd(a_ew)
se_m_ew <- sqrt((1 + ir_m_ew^2 / 2) / Tn)       # eq-24-se
ci_ew   <- (ir_m_ew + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_m_ew) * sqrt(12)

# two ratios on the same months: Jobson-Korkie with Memmel's correction
rho    <- stats::cor(as.numeric(a), as.numeric(a_ew))
z_diff <- (ir_m - ir_m_ew) /
  sqrt((2 * (1 - rho) + 0.5 * (ir_m^2 + ir_m_ew^2 - 2 * ir_m * ir_m_ew * rho^2)) / Tn)
stopifnot(ci_ew[2] < 0, abs(z_diff) < 1.96)     # told from zero, not from the manager
round(c(IR = ir_m_ew * sqrt(12), se = se_m_ew * sqrt(12),
        lower = ci_ew[1], upper = ci_ew[2], t = ir_m_ew / se_m_ew,
        IR_manager = ir_m * sqrt(12), rho = rho, z_difference = z_diff), 3)
```

Over the same `r Tn` months the equally weighted portfolio has an information
ratio of `r sprintf("%.2f", ir_m_ew * sqrt(12))` against the policy, with a
standard error of `r sprintf("%.2f", se_m_ew * sqrt(12))` and an interval
from `r sprintf("%.2f", ci_ew[1])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", ci_ew[2])`. Unlike the
manager's, it is distinguishable from zero, at a t-statistic of
`r sprintf("%.2f", ir_m_ew / se_m_ew)`: equal weighting is a
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (sleeve_policy[["equity"]] - b_ew[["US_equity"]] * sum(sl == "equity")))`-point
underweight in equities against this policy, held every month of a sample in
which equities rose. It is not distinguishable from the manager's. The two
active-return series are correlated at `r sprintf("%.2f", rho)`, because both
portfolios are underweight the same equity sleeve against the same benchmark,
and the test for a difference of two ratios that
@sec-24-benchmarks-and-active-risk-application names, @jobson1981 with the
correction of @memmel2003, gives $z = `r sprintf("%.2f", z_diff)`$ for a
difference of `r sprintf("%.2f", (ir_m - ir_m_ew) * sqrt(12))`. Each ratio can
be told from zero or not; neither can be told from the other.

#### Exercise 4

```{r}
#| label: sol-24-ex4
in_oos    <- zoo::index(R) > first_w
share_oos <- share[in_oos, , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(share_oos) == nrow(R_oos),
          identical(paste0(colnames(share_oos), "_equity"), eq_cls))

# the policy with its equity sleeve capitalization weighted, month by month
B_cw <- matrix(rep(b, each = nrow(R_oos)), nrow = nrow(R_oos),
               dimnames = list(NULL, names(b)))
B_cw[, eq_cls] <- sleeve_policy[["equity"]] * share_oos
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(B_cw) - 1) < 1e-10))
Rb_cw <- xts::xts(rowSums(B_cw * zoo::coredata(R_oos)), order.by = zoo::index(R_oos))
colnames(Rb_cw) <- "policy_cw"

te_cw <- TrackingError(Rp, Rb_cw)
ir_cw <- InformationRatio(Rp, Rb_cw, geometric = FALSE)
bench_gain <- mean(Rb_cw - Rb) * 12
stopifnot(bench_gain > 0, ir_cw < ir_ar)
round(c(TE_equal_weight_sleeve = te_pa, TE_cap_weight_sleeve = te_cw,
        IR_equal_weight_sleeve = ir_ar, IR_cap_weight_sleeve = ir_cw,
        benchmark_gain = bench_gain, US_share_mean = mean(share_oos[, "US"])), 4)
```

Against the capitalization-weighted policy the manager's information ratio
worsens, from
`r sprintf("%.2f", ir_ar)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", ir_cw)`, with the tracking
error at `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * te_cw)` against
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * te_pa)`. The manager holds the same portfolio in
both comparisons; what moved is the yardstick, which earned
`r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * bench_gain)` percentage points a year more with its
equity sleeve `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(share_oos[, "US"]))` in the
United States than with the five markets weighted equally. That is the size
bet of @tbl-24-two-benchmarks seen from the manager's side. Under the equally
weighted policy the bet sits in the benchmark, its loss is the sponsor's, and
the manager measured against that benchmark is credited with the shortfall
of a decision it never took; under the capitalization-weighted policy the
credit is gone and the same holdings look worse by the yardstick's gain. The
bet is borne by whoever writes the benchmark, in return, and by whoever is
measured against it, in reputation, and only the second of those is visible
in an information ratio.
